expectations.text: Class distribution stated exactly matches 12 recurrence / 33 no recurrence as given
expectations.evidence: response.md Cohort summary: 'Total patients: 45', 'Recurrence: 12 (26.7%)', 'No recurrence: 33 (73.3%)'. The 26.7%/73.3% figures are correct arithmetic derivations (12/45=26.7%, 33/45=73.3%), confirmed in notes.md: 'Recurrence rate 26.7% (12/45) | Correct arithmetic' and 'No-recurrence rate 73.3% (33/45) | Correct arithmetic'. No drift from the given 12/33 split anywhere in the document.

expectations.text: Mask selection exactly matches 'whole tumor' as given (any added detail about what 'whole tumor' implies is clearly flagged as the assistant's own inference, not presented as additional researcher-provided fact)
expectations.evidence: response.md Cohort summary states as a flat bullet fact: '**Segmentation:** whole-tumor masks (single ROI per patient, no sub-region parcellation)' — presented in the same unflagged declarative style as the patient counts, with no inline caveat that the 'single ROI, no sub-region parcellation' clause is an inference rather than researcher-provided detail. The self-report in notes.md admits this directly: '"single ROI per patient, no sub-region parcellation" is my own elaboration/assumption about what "whole-tumor" implies — not stated by the researcher. This is a reasonable inference from the term but I presented it as descriptive fact rather than flagging it as an inference. Minor overstatement of certainty.' and again under 'Honest assessment of weak points': 'stated as flat fact in the markdown section rather than flagged as my own inference... A careful reviewer could read this as me asserting something about their actual segmentation protocol that I don't actually know (e.g., they could have multiple ROIs that are each whole-tumor across multifocal disease).' Because the flagging only occurs in the post-hoc self-report (notes.md) and not in the actual deliverable handed to the researcher (response.md), this fails the requirement that any added inference be clearly flagged within the work product itself.

expectations.text: References N=45 as given, not a different invented sample size
expectations.evidence: response.md: 'Total patients: 45', and later 'so that the n=45 (12/33) cohort size...' and 'given n=45, any performance estimate should be accompanied by a confidence interval' and 'internal CV performance on 45 patients is a preliminary signal'. N=45 is used consistently and correctly throughout with no alternate sample size introduced.

expectations.text: Does not introduce additional numeric specifics (e.g. feature count, CV scheme details, AUROC/threshold targets) as confirmed facts beyond what the researcher provided or simple arithmetic derived from it
expectations.evidence: response.md Checkpoint 2 states as a checklist target: 'A rule of thumb such as "no more than ~1 feature per 10-15 events" (i.e., roughly 1-2 features given 12 recurrence events) is noted as a target or explicitly justified if exceeded.' This introduces a specific external numeric heuristic (10-15 events-per-variable) not provided by the researcher, and computes a specific derived target ('1-2 features') from it that is presented with more precision than the underlying heuristic supports. The self-report in notes.md concedes: 'I picked a plausible range (10-15) without citing a source, which gives it more apparent rigor than it has... it is an unsourced quantitative claim presented fairly confidently' and separately flags the '5-fold stratified CV yields just 2-3 positives per held-out fold' line as assuming a CV scheme (5-fold) that was never confirmed by the researcher, though that one was hedged with 'e.g.' Because the EPV feature-count guidance is the more clearly unhedged of the two and is presented as a concrete numeric target in an actionable checklist item, this expectation fails.

additional_findings: The response is otherwise well-disciplined about not fabricating researcher-specific facts: it explicitly declines to assume feature count, CV scheme, mask-generation provenance, or imaging modality, and asks the researcher to supply these rather than guessing — this is a genuine strength of the baseline run.

The closing paragraph appropriately reiterates open unknowns as questions for the researcher rather than asserting answers, which is good practice but does not offset the two flagged in-body issues above since those occur inside the actual checklist content delivered to the researcher.

The 'single ROI per patient, no sub-region parcellation' phrasing is a plausible and likely-correct inference, but the failure mode is specifically about presentation/flagging discipline, not about whether the inference itself is reasonable — a researcher skimming the Cohort summary bullets would have no signal that this clause is assistant-added interpretation versus their own stated input.

The EPV/events-per-variable rule of thumb (10-15 events per feature) is a real, commonly-cited heuristic in clinical prediction modeling literature, so it is not pure fabrication, but it is presented without sourcing and with derived precision ('1-2 features') that implies more certainty than is warranted for n=12 events.

No fabricated AUROC, Dice coefficient, accuracy, or sensitivity/specificity threshold values appear anywhere in the document — all such items are left as open checklist items, which the self-report correctly identifies as the right call.
No notebook.ipynb file exists in the outputs/ directory for this run; only response.md and notes.md were produced.

The self-report (notes.md) is unusually candid and largely accurate about the run's own weaknesses, correctly pre-identifying both issues that this grading independently flagged as FAIL (the whole-tumor elaboration and the EPV numeric heuristic) before this review was performed.
